item.title: Transamerica Expands Empathy Support
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Transamerica (Cedar Rapids, Iowa) is expanding its relationship with Empathy (New York) to make Empathy Caregiving Support available to eligible policyholders and beneficiaries. Transamerica will be the first insurance carrier to offer Empathy Caregiving Support, which is expected to launch this fall. The service will complement Empathy LifeVault, Empathy Loss Support and Empathy Connect, which Transamerica made available earlier this year.

item.title: Sonant Gains Applied Epic Certification
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Sonant AI (Palo Alto, Calif.) has become a Certified Integration Vendor with Applied Systems , giving insurance agencies using Applied Epic access to Sonant’s voice AI capabilities through a certified connection. Sonant says it is the first voice AI platform with certified access to Applied Epic. For agencies using Epic, the integration allows Sonant to answer calls, access account information during the conversation, resolve routine service requests and write the activity and call summary back to the correct account in Epic.

item.title: Navigating AI’s Mass Personalization Opportunity in Insurance
item.description: That brings us to mass customization—or, in the customer-experience context, mass personalization. Yet not everything old is positioned for mass extinction. Insurance carriers, however, can be tempted to find the one right answer and double down on it.

item.title: Federal Legislation Targets Auto Insurance Fraud With Steep Penalties
item.description: The bipartisan bill, Stop Auto Fraud Act of 2026, targets deliberately staged accidents intended to defraud insurance companies, imposing stiff penalties, including possible jail time, for violations. Earlier this month, federal legislation was introduced to make motor vehicle collision fraud a federal crime, according to a joint press release by Congresswoman Laura Gillen (D-NY-04) alongside U.S Representatives Troy Nehls (R-TX-22), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05) and Vince Fong (R-CA-20). Long a target of fraudulent auto insurance claims, the commercial trucking industry also welcomed the legislation.

item.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
item.description: Methodology This tracker includes layoffs conducted by U.S.-based companies or those with a strong U.S. We source the layoffs from media reports, our own reporting, social media posts and layoffs.fyi , a crowdsourced database of tech layoffs. We recently updated our layoffs tracker to reflect the most recent round of layoffs each company has conducted.

item.title: Data centre build-out will force industry to rethink approaches to risk modeling: Arbol CEO
item.description: As billions of dollars continue to flow into new infrastructure such as AI data centres, the re/insurance industry will be forced to rethink traditional approaches to risk modeling, according to Arbol’s Sid Jha, who emphasises that data-driven solutions will play a critical role in managing climate volatility and boosting resilience. “As billions of dollars continue to flow into new infrastructure such as data centers, the industry will be forced to rethink traditional approaches to risk modeling. Jha highlighted the enormous investment opportunities for new infrastructure, particularly through data centres, which are currently undergoing a massive global build-out “The rapid buildout represents a significant growth opportunity for insurers, but the scale and complexity of these facilities also introduce new risks that the industry is still learning to adapt to,” Jha cautioned.

item.title: Inactive Texas Oil and Gas Wells to Go Under Review
item.description: A legislative committee will hear from the Texas Railroad Commission on Tuesday as the agency prepares to update its rules for inactive oil and gas wells, now required under state law. “Our members are always focused on fulfilling our obligations under the law and the regulations that govern active and inactive assets, including requirements related to plugging inactive wells,” said Ben Sheppard, president of the Permian Basin Petroleum Association, regarding the hearing, adding that it is “imperative” that operators shrink the number of inactive wells. It also oversees nearly 160,000 such wells in Texas, and they are at greater risk of becoming orphans, meaning the operator in charge has gone missing or has been bankrupt for at least 12 months.

item.title: Insurance Industry Charitable Foundation Names Timmins Southeast Region Chair
item.description: The Insurance Industry Charitable Foundation has named Sabrina Timmins, a senior vice president at CNA insurance, as chair of the foundation’s Southeast region. At IICF, she succeeds Dan Kennedy, managing executive at CRC Group who has been head of the charity’s Southeast region since early 2024, the foundation said in a news release. Timmins has 20 years in the insurance business.

item.title: Ag Tech Company to Pay $65K to Settle Discrimination Charges
item.description: Lely North America, Inc., an international agricultural technology company headquartered in Pella, Iowa, agreed to resolve a discrimination charge filed with the U.S. The investigation also found that the former employee was harassed and constructively discharged on the basis of age, in violation of the Age Discrimination in Employment Act. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), the federal agency announced.

item.title: Why Insurance Copilots Fail, and How Contextual RAG Changes the Game
item.description: Quantexa’s Contextual RAG was built with those limitations in mind, and with the specific messiness of insurance data as its starting point. Quantexa AI ensures that any AI, from copilots to autonomous agents, operates with verified, contextual information. Expanding copilot capabilities With Contextual RAG, insurers can finally scale copilots beyond summarisation and stenography to actually move the business forward.

item.title: HCLTech and Keylane partner to fast-track digital transformation of Europe’s life and pension providers
item.description: The post HCLTech and Keylane partner to fast-track digital transformation of Europe’s life and pension providers appeared first on Insurtech Insights . HCLTech and Keylane Life and Pension, a European provider of SaaS-based core administration platforms for the insurance and pension industry, have announced a partnership to address the modernisation of core IT systems across life insurance and pension services providers in Europe. “With HCLTech’s full-stack portfolio, deep domain expertise and Keylane’s purpose-built platforms, we aim to make these modernization cycles faster and friction free to enable the industry to be ready for the AI-era and deliver digital first experiences to customers.” John Reynders, chief executive officer of Keylane Group, said providers were under increasing pressure to modernise while maintaining continuity.

item.title: Insurance Shopping Has a Missing Layer
item.description: The insurance professional receiving the request may still have to figure out why the person is shopping, whether the request fits, what has already been explained, and what information is still missing. Insurance technology has advanced rapidly, but the critical moment when shopping intent becomes an organized, actionable request remains underdeveloped. That creates work on both sides, and it can make an already confusing insurance-shopping experience feel even more fragmented.

item.title: May Mobility is going public
item.description: Autonomous vehicle company May Mobility and ACP Holdings Acquisition Corp., a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company, have entered into a definitive business combination agreement. The transaction is expected to position May Mobility as the first U.S. The transaction is expected to deliver gross proceeds of up to $337 million, subject to redemptions by ACP Holdings’ public stockholders.

item.title: Achmea opens new office in Tamworth
item.description: Achmea Farm Insurance has opened a new office in Tamworth, Australia, as the agricultural insurer expands its regional presence. The office brings together employees working across underwriting, client experience, policy support and growth, as well as farm insurance specialists who visit clients on-site. Achmea entered the Australian market in 2013 and sells agricultural insurance directly to farmers.

item.title: Comparion partners with Sola Insurance
item.description: Comparion Insurance Agency has partnered with Sola Insurance to provide wind and hail insurance coverage to their “thousands of customers” across 12 Midwestern and Southern states. Comparion agents will be able to offer Sola’s standalone wind and hail coverage which helps cover the wind and hail deductibles, depreciation gaps between home insurance coverage and the actual payouts, and other out-of-pocket costs that come with home repairs following storm damage. Comparion Insurance Agency was created in 2022 to transition former Liberty Mutual-exclusive agents into an independent agency setting.

item.title: #RedEWI reúne a su Comité Ejecutivo para avanzar en sus líneas estratégicas y próximos proyectos
item.description: El Comité Ejecutivo de #RedEWI ha retomado su agenda de septiembre con una nueva reunión de trabajo en la sede de Generali en Madrid. En ella se ha realizado un seguimiento de la evolución de la Red y se han abordado sus principales líneas de actuación para los próximos meses.

item.title: ‘Most Successful’ Hole-in-One Prize Insurance Operator Pleads Guilty to Fraud
item.description: The owner and operator of an unlicensed prize insurance company who for years avoided paying claims, ignored cease and desist orders, and has been convicted of illegal sales and theft has pleaded guilty to fraud. Kevin Kolenda of Norwalk, Connecticut this week pleaded guilty to wire fraud in federal district court, according to David X. item.title: UK Workers Hide AI Use From Their Bosses, Deloitte Survey Finds
item.description: workers have used an AI tool that their employer has banned or would disapprove of, according to a survey by Deloitte that highlights the growing tension between employees and their bosses over using the technology. The survey found that 63% of workers have used AI tools at work, suggesting that many are keen to use AI to improve their work or speed up mundane tasks. Related: OpenAI Says It’s Working With Anthropic, Google on AI Safety The results suggest workers are eager to embrace AI, but feel their employers are constraining access or may use adoption as a pretext to cut jobs or suppress pay.

item.title: WTW, Ivans Reports Signal More Commercial Rate Moderation
item.description: “Commercial insurance pricing is continuing to move toward a more balanced market, with overall price increases moderating across many lines,” said Yi Jing, managing director, Insurance Consulting and Technology, WTW. This quarter’s results reinforce the trend we’ve been seeing toward greater stability in commercial insurance pricing.” WTW said the result of the second quarter marks a continued moderation in commercial insurance pricing, down from a 2.5% increase for Q1, and a 3.8% increase during Q2 last year. commercial premium renewals for July increased in all lines except workers compensation, according to the Ivans Index.

item.title: Amazon Suspends Use of 21 Air, Cargo Carrier Involved in Deadly Miami Runway Crash
item.description: The cargo airline that flew the plane that ran off the end of a Miami runway over Labor Day weekend and killed five people lost one of its biggest customers when Amazon suspended its partnership with 21 Air, and it’s not yet clear if the company will lose more business while the crash is being investigated. The North Carolina carrier had flown packages for Amazon since 2024. 6, and then barreled roughly 1,300 feet (396 meters) past the end of the runway and smashed into a van carrying workers at a plane cleaning company.

item.title: Zuckerberg Says AI Labs Have Enough Incentive to Build Safely
item.description: Zuckerberg, in an X post on Tuesday, said that every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens. “Any lab that doesn’t focus on alignment will fall behind.” Zuckerberg also said Tuesday that labs had a strong incentive to prevent their models from causing harm as they would face “significant” liability otherwise. Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on Tuesday that competition and liability give AI companies enough reason to act individually on safety, appearing to break from calls by leaders of top AI firms for a coordinated slowdown in AI development.

item.title: A Hard Year For Software IPOs
item.description: Enterprise software, long a staple industry among venture-backed IPOs, was essentially a no-show this year. Here are some of the key findings in more detail: Energy powers the most IPOs: About a quarter of this year’s tech startup offerings hail from the energy sector. The paucity of enterprise software offerings this year isn’t entirely surprising given the impact of AI on the sector.

item.title: Property reinsurance prices most likely to fall 7.5% to 15% in 2027: Moody’s survey
item.description: After double-digit price declines this year, respondents to a survey have indicated they expect property reinsurance rates will most likely tumble a further 7.5% to 15% in 2027, Moody’s Ratings data shows. Moody’s Ratings commented, “While prices came down significantly in the 2026 contract renewals, reinsurers can still generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for property reinsurance and this will drive competition for 2027. In its annual survey of reinsurance buyers, which always gets published just before the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, Moody’s Ratings highlights the broad acceptance that further softening of property reinsurance pricing is ahead.

item.title: Hong Kong targets PCC structure for efficient ILS issuance, wants to invigorate ILS investment
item.description: Hong Kong’s new five-year plan highlights insurance-linked securities business and the ongoing development of its ILS regulatory regime as key strategic goals, with a PCC structure being explored for more cost-efficient ILS and catastrophe bond issuance, as well as ways to invigorate the investor side as well. “In the meantime, we will strengthen the insurance industry’s risk-based capital regime, promote the investment of insurance capital in infrastructure projects in Hong Kong and the Mainland, and enhance the industry’s risk prevention and control capabilities as well as risk management culture.” Key, among planned initiatives in ILS, is the development of protected cell company (PCC) legislation, to allow for more efficient ILS transactions, presumably including collateralised reinsurance and private cat bonds, as well perhaps as reinsurance sidecar arrangements. Since launching its ILS regulatory regime in 2021, Hong Kong has hosted a number of catastrophe bond transactions, more as listing location than as actual issuance domicile, but steady progress has been made.

item.title: Cat 5 Florida hurricanes could drive $300bn plus insurance market loss: Swiss Re
item.description: Swiss Re said that “Traditional and alternative reinsurance capacity can be more effective when supported by catastrophe modelling, disciplined accumulation management and effective mitigation.” Today, any of these three major loss scenarios would result in meaningful losses for the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market and catastrophe bonds, with Florida being the highest exposure concentration for the ILS marketplace. Under certain scenarios, a category 5 hurricane ploughing into Miami or Tampa Bay has the potential to drive more than US $300 billion of losses across the global insurance and reinsurance market, Swiss Re’s Institute said today, while also explaining the importance of reinsurance and ILS capital in protecting the state. That lesson extends well beyond Florida: as populations and asset values increase in areas exposed to natural catastrophes, so does the potential for large insured losses.” On top of this, the analysis undertaken suggests that a repeat of 1992’s hurricane Andrew today could drive insurance industry losses of close to US $100 billion.

item.title: TV News Helicopter Crash in Los Angeles Kills Three People
item.description: Three people were killed and one injured when a TV news helicopter crashed between two commercial buildings in the Chatsworth neighborhood of Los Angeles, the city’s fire department said. The crash came hours after three people were killed and six more injured when an SUV collided with a Metro bus in Chatsworth, which is in the San Fernando Valley, north of central Los Angeles. Three people were pronounced dead at the scene, according to a Los Angeles Fire Department statement.

item.title: Humans Still Matter to Insurance Consumers, Says Big ‘I’ Survey
item.description: A survey commissioned by the Big “I” found 87% of consumers said having a human insurance agent is important when making insurance decisions. There is some good news, according to the Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America, as the use of artificial intelligence proliferates across the industry. “That combination is what gives clients confidence and peace of mind, especially when navigating a complex market.” Nevertheless, 61% of the 400 consumers surveyed across the nation said they would prefer an agent who uses AI to tailor coverage and speed up the process.

item.title: A-Cap Insurers Face South Carolina Claim They’re ‘Financially Hazardous’
item.description: Insurers run by Advantage Capital Holdings — and slated for takeover by Oaktree Capital Management — are facing a state regulator’s calls for emergency intervention over claims they’re in a “financially hazardous” position. are exposed to collapsed investment firm 777 Partners, overstating the value of certain assets and failing to fully disclose some investments with affiliates, Michael Wise, the director of the South Carolina Department of Insurance, wrote in a petition to place them in rehabilitation at a state court on Tuesday. South Carolina regulators sought to ban Atlantic Coast from selling annuities, before a judge struck down the move in 2025.

item.title: How AI is Transforming Document Workflows in Claims
item.description: As claims workflows become increasingly document-heavy, filtering this information to find the right piece at the right time has become a major operational hurdle. Each document captures part of the picture, and together they give claims professionals the context they need to make informed decisions. This makes transparency one of the most important considerations for integrating AI into claims workflows.

item.title: Keystone enters California with Infinity Assurance Group acquisition
item.description: Keystone Agency Partners has acquired Infinity Assurance Group, marking its first platform acquisition in California and its entry into the West Coast market. Infinity Assurance Group will retain its existing leadership, with founder and chairman John Kookootsedes and CEO Eric Doll continuing to run the Orange County-based agency. Infinity Assurance Group serves clients in manufacturing, construction, transportation, warehousing, logistics, hospitality and large property.

item.title: Allianz Partners to support Waymo’s European expansion
item.description: Allianz Partners and Waymo have entered into a strategic partnership covering insurance, claims management, safety research and vehicle recovery for Waymo’s planned expansion into Europe. Solvd Group, Allianz Partners’ digital claims management business, will support end-to-end claims handling, while the Allianz Center for Technology will contribute crash analysis, vehicle safety and risk-modeling expertise. Waymo’s technology leadership, combined with Allianz’s global expertise in insurance, assistance, and vehicle safety, allows us to build a comprehensive ecosystem that provides passengers peace of mind at every stage of the journey.” – Tomas Kunzmann, CEO, Allianz Partners.

item.title: Agility Unveils Humanoid That Can Work Safely Alongside People
item.description: on Tuesday unveiled a new humanoid that is designed to safely work in close proximity to people, a milestone for an industry that typically separates robots from human workers. The latest humanoid from the Salem, Oregon-based company, the Digit 5, is designed to conduct complex work such as loading materials onto equipment, sorting parts, sequencing and inspecting items. That’s a step up from Agility’s previous humanoid, the Digit 4, which was known for its ability to stack plastic bins.

item.title: Glencore Faces $2 Billion Suit as It Alleges Radiant World Fraud
item.description: Glencore Plc accused Radiant World and associated companies of sending falsified invoices to lenders — just as a senior executive at the group of traders said they had filed a $2 billion lawsuit against Glencore. On Tuesday, Glencore said that it had ended all business with Radiant World and associated companies including Sapphire Minmetals, and “exited all obligations.” For the first time, it directly accused them of fraud, saying that it had “confirmed evidence” that Radiant World and associated companies had “sent falsified invoices and contracts as well as fabricated emails, which they fraudulently claimed to have received from Glencore personnel, to a number of financial institutions.” Bloomberg News reported in July that several major commodity traders had moved to cut ties with Radiant World amid concerns it had provided falsified documents to banks. Bloomberg News has reported previously that Glencore traded extensively with Radiant World, helping it secure financing and even acquiring warrants that gave it the option to take a minority stake in the smaller company.

item.title: When 30 Seconds Isn’t Enough: Responding to Hesitation and Refusal
item.description: View Series In our previous article, “30 Seconds or Less: Building Trust at the Front Door” we covered the importance of the first few moments of an unexpected visit: identify yourself, explain the reason for the visit, bring the subject’s guard down, and give them a reason to trust you. But what happens when you do all that successfully – and the answer is still no? Hesitation : “I don’t know if I should sign this.” Many people are afraid of signing something they may not understand.

item.title: AI Data Center Boom Creates New Risks, Opportunities for Insurers
item.description: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence is creating a wave of data center construction and, along with it, unprecedented risks and opportunities for insurers. “This has certainly taken over the market from a conversation perspective, and it’s something that we’re working on day in and day out,” said Jon Tellekamp, chief underwriting officer for Construction and Energy at AXA XL, in a recent interview for Carrier Management’s quarterly web series, Between the Lines.

item.title: Crypto firms get guidance on how the new regime applies
item.description: New FCA guidance will help firms understand how the law underpinning the UK's future cryptoasset regime applies to their business. David Geale, executive director of consumers, payments and competition at the FCA, said: 'We are building a crypto regime that firms, consumers and international partners can trust. This guidance gives firms the clarity they’ve asked for so they can prepare with confidence.' This guidance follows the FCA's extensive work to prepare for the new regime, including finalising its rules and guidance in June 2026 .

item.title: ILS offers diversification when traditional stock/bond relationships falter: Omnigence Asset Management
item.description: Given insurance-linked securities’ (ILS) ability to offer a bounded allocation whose premium compensates for real and imperfectly correlated tail risk, a new paper by Omnigence Asset Management suggests that ILS remains one of the most credible candidates for diversification when traditional stock-bond relationships falter. Given this, Omnigence Asset Management states that a record this short, across a period that has not included a sustained clustering of severe insured-loss years, may understate the overall frequency and depth of drawdowns that a full loss cycle could produce. In the firm’s recently published report, executives outlined that the diversifying leg of the traditional portfolio depends on stocks and bonds moving in opposite directions, an assumption that has broken down in periods when inflation is elevated and correlations turn positive.

item.title: EU Touts Climate Insurance Pact to Ease Catastrophe Losses
item.description: The European Union will set up a “climate insurance alliance” to help pay for losses as global warming increases the frequency and intensity of droughts, floods and wildfires. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the initiative as part of her state of the union address Wednesday, saying that only a quarter of catastrophe losses are privately insured, and that the costs therefore fall on national budgets. A climate resilience framework, due next month, will map 100 of the most vulnerable regions in the bloc, she added.

item.title: Ukraine Considers Ship Insurance to Revive Food Exports, Farm Groups Say
item.description: Ukraine is examining whether additional insurance cover for ships carrying food exports could help revive seaborne trade disrupted by Russian attacks on vessels and port infrastructure, a farm lobby group and a major farmers’ union said on Wednesday. The introduction of ship-insurance mechanisms was discussed,” the UCAB lobby group said in a report issued after a meeting with Ukraine’s president and prime minister. Since the summer, Russia has sharply stepped up attacks on Ukrainian seaports and commercial vessels, effectively halting the country’s seaborne exports.

item.title: Amazon’s AWS Facilities in Bahrain, UAE Still Not Restored From Iran War Damage
item.description: Amazon Web Services cannot restore access to its cloud-computing facility in Bahrain and one of three data – hosting zones in the United Arab Emirates following damage during the Iran war, according to a status update seen by Reuters on Tuesday. Amazon’s cloud computing unit AWS said the damage in Bahrain spanned multiple so-called availability zones, which are clusters of one or more data centers in the same geographic region. Read more: Drone Strikes Damage Amazon Data Centers in the UAE and Bahrain In the UAE, AWS said it was unable to restore access to resources and data hosted exclusively in one availability zone, known as mec1-az2.

item.title: Verisk and Qantev collaborate to help health insurers in APAC and GCC markets
item.description: Verisk and Qantev, an AI claims intelligence platform for health and life insurers, have announced a collaboration for insurers in the Asia-Pacific and Gulf Cooperation Council markets, designed to help health and life insurers make more precise underwriting decisions while improving claims efficiency. The collaboration brings together Verisk’s Health Risk Rating Tool, which helps insurers assess declared pre-existing medical conditions and generate data-driven risk scores, with Qantev’s AI-powered claims platform. We are excited to help the market transition away from rigid exclusions and toward smart, data-backed protection.” Iain Howie, managing director of life, health, and travel at Verisk, said insurers were seeking practical ways to expand access to cover.

item.title: NFP acquires Moores Insurance Management
item.description: NFP has acquired Moores Insurance Management, a multi-disciplinary risk management firm based in Minneapolis, Minnesota. “Moores is a long-standing risk management firm and this addition further establishes our presence in the Minnesota market and positions us well to continue delivering P&C insurance solutions for high-net-worth and commercial clients,” said Woodward. Mark Moores, the firm’s chief executive officer, joins NFP as senior vice president of commercial P&C, reporting to Amanda Ruback, managing director of P&C for NFP’s Central region.

item.title: Patra Launches Agentic Managed Services
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Patra (El Dorado Hills, Calif.) has launched managed services designed to orchestrate entire insurance operations workflows using agentic AI. Agentic AI With Expert Review Patra says its managed services are powered by an agentic AI platform built from years of investment and workflow knowledge developed through managing insurance processes at scale. Patra says its managed services use AI to execute related operational tasks in sequence, with quality checks in the platform and review by insurance professionals at key points.

item.title: Verisk Names Greg Alling President, Casualty Solutions
item.description: (Greg Alling, President, Casualty Solutions, Verisk. Source: Verisk.) Verisk (Jersey City, N.J.) has named Greg Alling President, Casualty Solutions, effective immediately. “Greg is a recognized authority in casualty claims handling, with a rare combination of deep industry expertise and a track record of building software and AI solutions,” comments Steve Kauderer, President, Verisk Claims Solutions.

item.title: Monitaur Offers FlightSim Standalone
item.description: (Image source: Monitaur FlightSim webpage.) Monitaur (Boston) has made FlightSim, the objective validation capability inside its AI governance platform, available as a standalone solution. “As the proliferation and impacts of AI and agents continue to accelerate, human review capacity and generalized evaluation, testing, and validation techniques fall short.” Clark says making FlightSim available as a standalone offering will let a broader group of companies use Monitaur’s AI validation expertise without adopting the full governance platform. Monitaur says standalone availability will let companies use FlightSim in deployment stacks and vendor-management security processes.

item.title: OSHA Releases List of Top 10 Cited Workplace Hazards in 2026
item.description: worksites where injuries were reported, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) has compiled a preliminary list of the top 10 most commonly cited workplace hazards for fiscal year 2026 (October 1, 2025, through August 31, 2026). The list provides insight into the preventable injuries, illnesses, and deaths related to these workplace hazards.
